name: veh_speed_MON_128
comment: EGAS-L2 MONITOR ego speed, 1/128 km/h (= veh_speed_FUNC_100 * 32/25). All L2 monitor speed compares are cal_u8_kmh * 0x80 (=*128). NOTE: not every '* 0x80' in these monitors is a speed compare - torque/accel values are also scaled *0x40/*0x80.

name: veh_speed_FUNC_100
comment: FUNCTIONAL ego speed (core ctx0), 0.01 km/h. The functional ACC path uses this; the L2 monitors use veh_speed_MON_128 instead.

name: veh_speed_FUNC_100_ctx1
comment: Functional ego speed, core ctx1 twin of veh_speed_FUNC_100 (0.01 km/h).

name: cru_acc_active_flag
comment: Cruise/ACC-active operating flag (= d000abfc, written by the 0x8031 ACC/DCC state block via FUN_801915ce). GATES the #208 cruise-speed monitor: its floor/latch only runs when cruise/ACC is the active longitudinal controller. This is what makes #208 ACC-specific.

name: MON_acc_long_setpoint
comment: Monitor-domain copy of the cruise/ACC longitudinal setpoint (LSB x0x40), built by FUN_800e37de from the GRA/cruise setpoint block (802c4ee8 <- d0008980/84). Bounded by the #213 monitor (800f4abe) inside speed/dwell rails; shared input across the L2 monitor cluster.

name: EGAS_L2_cru_speed_monitor_A
comment: *** THE genuine ACC min-speed monitor (EGAS-L2 cruise/ACC speed-control plausibility, C_VS_MIN_CRU_MON). Gated on cru_acc_active_flag (d000a113). *** Over cal #208 @0x803896ec. Builds MON_cru_permit_flags (d000d7d1) via the persistent permit memory dc87; OPERATIVE FLOOR = 15-SET (0x80389809) / 7-CLEAR (0x8038980e) -> bit7. BEHAVIOUR: SELF-RECOVERING speed-gated PERMIT -- below the floor with dc87=0 the permit is withheld (ECU does not apply the ACC command), and it re-arms/resumes the moment speed>15 (MED17 openpilot user sees re-enable at ~15 = the SET edge). NOT a key-off-on lockout (that is the Simos); #208 feeds NONE of the torque-limp aggregator bytes and the corpus has no NV/Dem store. d00148be is only the monitor-ENGAGED latch. Fix: set both floor cells to 0.

name: EGAS_L2_cru_speed_monitor_B
comment: Continuation/second pass of EGAS_L2_cru_speed_monitor_A over the same cal #208 (Ghidra-split; enters on live registers). Re-derives the 15/7 floor into MON_cru_permit_flags bit7; shares latch d00148be + counters d00148bf/d000d822.

name: MON_cru_speed_engaged_latch
comment: #208 cruise-speed-monitor ENGAGED latch (NOT the fault). Set 800f006c:793 when cru_acc_active_flag(d000a113) AND d000d7f2 (which includes permit-bit7-SET = *permitted*); CLEARED on cruise-off (a113=0) or recovery (d240==8). Monitor-active state, not a stored fault; all volatile RAM. Below the floor the permit is simply withheld (self-recovering, re-arms at speed>15) -- no key-off-on lockout on MED17 (that was the Simos). Exported as EGAS_mon_diag_status bit0x10 (a per-cycle mirror, zero internal readers).

name: EGAS_mon_diag_status
comment: Shared per-monitor diagnostic status bitfield (Dem status projection). bit0x10 (b4) = a per-cycle MIRROR of MON_cru_speed_engaged_latch (via getter 802184f2) = 'cru-speed monitor engaged', NOT a stored fault. Has ZERO internal readers; the ACC/ESP coordinator 801455ae reads only bits 0x40/0x04. NOT a stored fault: the corpus has no NV/Dem write for this bit, and #208's effect is a self-recovering permit withhold (re-arms at speed>15), not a lockout. The key-off-on hard lockout was the Simos, not MED17.

name: MON_cru_permit_floor_flag
comment: L2 monitor PERSISTENT permit memory: 'vehicle has been in the cruise-speed range'. SET when veh_speed_MON_128 > 15 (0x80389809); CLEARED when speed < 7 (0x8038980e); HOLDS between. Written ONLY in the floor block (800f006c:742 / 800f027c:656), reset NOWHERE -> persists across latch cycles + ACC on/off (zeroed only at key-on). Updated only while the monitor is un-latched (arming phase). -> MON_cru_permit_flags bit7; on the next cycle it arms MON_cru_speed_engaged_latch. The 15 = arm-from-scratch, the 7 = re-arm floor (both live).

name: MON_cru_permit_flags
comment: #208 monitor's private cru-permit bitfield (referenced only in 800f006c/027c). bit7 = MON_cru_permit_floor_flag (15/7). The L2 half of the L1/L2 speed-control plausibility; feeds the d00148be latch, not the ACC control path directly.

name: MON_speed_above17_flag
comment: #208 companion band: SET when veh_speed_MON_128 > C_VS_MON_speed17_SET (0x8038980a=17); CLEARED below 17 - C_VS_MON_speed17_bandwidth2(0x80389808=2) = 15. -> d000d7de. SECONDARY arming window (not the operative floor).

name: MON_speed_17band_state
comment: Latched output of MON_speed_above17_flag (17/15). Secondary arming window for other #208 sub-checks; also read by #213 (800f4abe).

name: C_VS_MON_CRU_permit_SET_15
comment: cal #208 +0x11d, u8 km/h = 15. *** THE operative ACC min-speed lever -- the SET/ARM edge. *** EGAS_L2_cru_speed_monitor_A:737 veh_speed_MON_128 > 15*128 -> permit bit7=1 -> the engaged-latch ARMS. The 15/7 floor block runs ONLY while the latch=0 (:728); once armed it holds until ACC-off. The permit memory dc87 is persistent (never reset); with dc87=0 (fresh key-on below 15, or after dropping below 7) the latch never arms and the ACC command is withheld below 15. Set cal=0 -> dc87 arms at any speed>0. Set WITH CLR_7 (7->0, so dc87 never clears) for a re-engage-robust fix. Recompute cal checksum.

name: C_VS_MON_CRU_permit_CLR_7
comment: cal #208 +0x122, u8 km/h = 7. RE-ARM / memory-clear edge -- LIVE. 800f006c:742 `speed < 7*128` clears dc87 (MON_cru_permit_floor_flag), a PERSISTENT hysteretic memory (SET at 15, CLEAR at 7, written only in the floor block, reset nowhere). dc87 holds across latch/ACC cycles, so once =1 you can drop and RE-ENGAGE ACC down to 7; below 7 (un-latched) dc87 clears -> must exceed 15 to re-arm. The floor block runs only while un-latched (arming phase), so this edge is live on every (re-)engagement. Set cal=0 -> dc87 never clears. Set with SET_15.

name: C_VS_MON_speed17_SET
comment: cal #208 +0x11e, u8 km/h = 17. SET edge of the secondary 17/15 band (MON_speed_above17_flag). Clear = 17 - 0x80389808(2) = 15. SECONDARY (arms other sub-checks), not the operative floor. Move with the primary floor for L1/L2 consistency if needed.

name: C_VS_MON_speed17_bandwidth2
comment: cal #208 +0x11c, u8 km/h = 2. Hysteresis BAND WIDTH (subtracted) for the 17-band -> clear edge 15. Relative band, leave stock.

name: EGAS_L2_ACC_longsetpoint_band_213
comment: ACC-relevant (indirect) EGAS-L2 monitor of the ACC/GRA longitudinal setpoint (cal #213 @0x8038a3c8). Bounds MON_acc_long_setpoint (d000d5aa) inside speed/dwell-dependent accel/torque rails (d000d832/d834); debounced sub-faults FEED #208 (d000d829/d82a/d842 -> 800f006c) and the aggregator (d83c/d/e -> FUN_800d9936 -> d344 -> aa23 -> 0x8031 ACC/DCC ctrl). GENUINE speed edges: 0x8038a4ec(=0, moving/standstill) and 0x8038a4ed(=25, sub-check enable). The cells 0x8038a4d7/d8/d9(=16/18/16) and 0x8038a4ee(=12) are torque/accel RAIL coefficients + hysteresis, NOT speed floors..

name: EGAS_L2_cru_lowspeed_crawl_215
comment: ACC-relevant (indirect) EGAS-L2 cruise/ACC low-speed CRAWL monitor (cal #215 @0x8038a568). Fault severity d000d857 -> cruise fault-reaction manager 800dca9c (can force fault/off via d000d3fc) + aggregator 800d9936. Two-stage state machine d000d858/d859 (cases 0-3). Its crawl trip runs ONLY in the failsafe branch (when internal signal 0x3fc is STALE - runs at startup/on-message-loss, NOT proven dead). Speed cells 0x8038a5c9/ca(=6)/cd(=5) are crawl ARMING windows, 0x8038a5c6(=20) an upper counter-reset bound, 0x8038a5cb(=0) DISABLES a d859 transition. Not an ACC engage floor..

name: EGAS_L2_fault_aggregator
comment: THE EGAS-Level-2 monitor DTC/fault aggregator. AND-masks ~8-15 monitor result bytes (from 800f25e2/800f40bc/800f5d68/800f5982/800f4abe/...) with cal enables into fault dwords d000d32c/d334/d338, computes overall verdict d000d344 (0-3 severity) -> d000aa23 (read by the 0x8031 ACC/DCC controller) = the EGAS-3 torque-limitation/limp reaction. Terminal sink for all L2 monitors.

name: EGAS_L2_fault_verdict
comment: Overall EGAS-L2 fault verdict/severity (0-3) from EGAS_L2_fault_aggregator. Copied to EGAS_L2_reaction_level (d000aa23) via FUN_802c51c2; drives the engine torque-limitation/limp reaction.

name: EGAS_L2_reaction_level
comment: = EGAS_L2_fault_verdict (d000d344). Read by the 0x8031 ACC/DCC controller functions (80312f70/803147dc/80315a54, mirrored to d000abed) - the ACC-facing effect of a confirmed L2 monitor fault (torque limp).

name: EGAS_L2_torque_monitor_209_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - general engine-torque EGAS-L2 plausibility (Momentenueberwachung), cal #209 @0x80389868. Compares model vs permitted torque, debounces faults into d000deea/deeb -> packed df0a-0d -> EGAS_L2_fault_aggregator. Speed cells 0x8038a205/206/207 (8/5/0) are torque-check low-speed windows; 0x8038a202-204 (255/255/254) DISABLE their speed gates. No ACC coupling.

name: EGAS_L2_torque_monitor_214_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - general EGAS-L2 torque-vs-speed plausibility, cal #214 @0x8038a514. 0x8038a551(=10) is a low-speed SUPPRESSION term for a torque check, not an ACC floor. Latches a held verdict d000d846 -> EGAS_L2_fault_aggregator. No ACC coupling.

name: EGAS_L2_torque_plaus_seq_173_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 sequential torque-plausibility, cal #173 @0x80385c4c. Its 0x8038679b(=15) is the LOWER BOUND of a torque-window [15,105] arming a corridor check on MON_acc_long_setpoint - a numerical coincidence, NOT the C_VS_MIN_CRU_MON floor. All state volatile, no non-volatile latch, no ACC var referenced. Do NOT edit for openpilot.

name: EGAS_L2_channel_plaus_211_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 redundant channel/pedal plausibility voting, cal #211 @0x8038a25a. 0x8038a3a4(=255) is a de-facto DISABLED 255 km/h over-speed ceiling; other speed uses are axis/threshold selects. Packs df2d/2e/2f -> EGAS_L2_fault_aggregator. No ACC coupling.

name: EGAS_L2_torque_coordinator_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 permitted-vs-actual longitudinal torque check. Enabled only in a 25-130 km/h driving window (the opposite of a low-speed floor). Sets monitor result d000e036. No ACC coupling.

name: EGAS_L2_accel_torque_model_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 longitudinal accel/torque MODEL. Vehicle speed is a MAP AXIS input, not a floor. Contains the MONITOR twin of the +/-500000 decel rail (the monitor's own authority, not the functional one). Outputs d000d5xx monitor group.

name: EGAS_L2_roadload_model_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 road-load/driving-resistance model: v^2 aero drag + v rolling + accel terms -> resistance shadows d000dfe2/e8 (feeds EGAS_L2_torque_coordinator 800fb796). Speed used as physical model axis, not a threshold.

name: EGAS_L2_step_dtc_manager_193_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 operating-step sequencer + DTC manager, cal #193 @0x80387f5c. 0x80387fbc(=6) gates only the internal step-active flag d000d6f7 in coast-state (SUPPRESSES the sequencer at low speed). No ACC var referenced.

name: EGAS_L2_torque_plaus_148_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 monitor-domain torque plausibility, cal #148 @0x8038436a. PROVABLY produces no low-speed fault: double-gated (subsystem-state d3cd in {3,8} + operating-point>=80, then hysteresis d000d867 SET>12 / CLEAR<5 via 0x80384761=5 low-edge + 0x80384760=7 band-width) -> self-disables below ~12 km/h. Outputs feed only telemetry+getter. No ACC coupling.

name: ACC_master_state_machine
comment: ACC/GRA master state machine. Transition table @0x80044772 (134 entries): a3c1 (ACC_master_mode, out_idx 0x1b) = a DIRECT COPY of cond[0x1c] = the 2-bit commanded mode. NO engine-side speed floor gates engagement; it relays the commanded ACC mode (openpilot via ACC_01).

name: statemachine_unpack_cond_vector
comment: Unpacks the 10-byte packed ACC condition vector into 50 condition slots (1-3 bits each). cond[0x1c]=byte5[5:6]=the 2-bit ACC mode -> ACC_master_mode.

name: statemachine_confirm_transition
comment: Transition-confirm layer over ACC_cond_vec_current (d0009b63) vs _new (d0009b70) via descriptor 0x8003f374. Event-driven; no speed compare.

name: statemachine_recv_cond_events
comment: Receives ACC engage-condition events via OS mailbox d0009b48 and packs them into the condition vector. Conditions arrive pre-computed; no speed literal.

name: ACC_cond_vec_current
comment: Current packed ACC engage-condition vector (10 bytes). byte5[5:6] = commanded ACC mode -> ACC_master_mode.

name: ACC_cond_vec_new
comment: Candidate/new packed ACC engage-condition vector; confirmed into ACC_cond_vec_current.

name: ACC_master_mode
comment: ACC/GRA master mode: 0=inactive,1=GRA,2=ACC,3=ACC-extended = direct copy of engage condition slot 0x1c. Feeds d000a454 via FUN_802c806e. No engine-side speed floor gates this.
